summary:
Research summary for documenting a FiveM MP-freemode clothing TEXTURE package (user context: "a jacket, pants and chain" -> slots jbib (11), lowr (4), teef (7)).

VERIFIED (fetched primary sources): component enum (citizenfx/natives), file-name grammar incl. race-suffix table and texture-letter indexing (CodeWalker MetaTypes.cs source), supported DDS/BC formats in YTD (CodeWalker DDSIO.cs), official fxmanifest keyword definitions incl. this_is_a_map wording (citizenfx/fivem-docs), official data_file types SHOP_PED_APPAREL_META_FILE / ALTERNATE_VARIATIONS_FILE (fivem-docs data-files.md), a real replacement pack (Zerofour04/FiveM-ClothingPack) and real add-on packs (drkkkkkk/StaffHoodie, TimyStream template, 80+ manifests found via GitHub code search) showing the exact layout, shop meta XML and manifest lines.

NOT DIRECTLY VERIFIABLE from this sandbox (egress-blocked: forum.cfx.re, docs.fivem.net, docs.altv.mp, gta5mod.net, docs.gta.clothing, modding-forum.com, gtaforums.com, openiv.org, gta5-mods.com, hifivem, fivemx, xgamingserver, fivemcoach, tebex blogs): the "1024x1024 max / 16 MB per YTD" community rules, OpenIV's PNG->DDS import dialog options, creaturemetadata semantics (heels / hide-hair), the alt:V tutorial text, and race ids 6/7/9 names. These are reported from search-result snippets or my own knowledge and are marked as such in each section. Whether the game engine (as opposed to CodeWalker) strictly requires the texture name inside the YTD to equal the file name could not be confirmed from engine source; the convention is to keep them identical and ship one texture per YTD.

Downloaded source files used for grep verification: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-momentum-motorsports/f27718b1-7c06-5fda-9f0a-8cc53aabc796/scratchpad/MetaTypes.cs, Ped.cs, DDSIO.cs (CodeWalker), voguev.md.
component_slots:
Component ids for SET_PED_COMPONENT_VARIATION(ped, componentId, drawableId, textureId, paletteId) — enum quoted from citizenfx/natives (PED/SetPedComponentVariation.md); file-name prefixes are CodeWalker's MCPVComponentData.ComponentTypeNames array (verified):

 id | enum (native label) | file prefix | what actually lives there (5mod-tutorials + SOZ README, verified)
 0  | PV_COMP_HEAD ("HEAD")        | head | head/face
 1  | PV_COMP_BERD ("BEARD")       | berd | masks / beards
 2  | PV_COMP_HAIR ("HAIR")        | hair | hair
 3  | PV_COMP_UPPR ("UPPER")       | uppr | torso/arms (the skin "torso" under the top)
 4  | PV_COMP_LOWR ("LOWER")       | lowr | legs -> PANTS / JEANS
 5  | PV_COMP_HAND ("HAND")        | hand | bags / parachutes (hands)
 6  | PV_COMP_FEET ("FEET")        | feet | shoes
 7  | PV_COMP_TEEF ("TEETH")       | teef | "Accessories": teeth/scarf/NECKLACE -> CHAINS, ties, scarves
 8  | PV_COMP_ACCS ("ACCESSORIES") | accs | UNDERSHIRTS (despite the enum label)
 9  | PV_COMP_TASK ("TASK")        | task | body armour
 10 | PV_COMP_DECL ("DECL")        | decl | decals / badges
 11 | PV_COMP_JBIB ("JBIB")        | jbib | tops / JACKETS / HOODIES
 (PV_COMP_MAX = 12)

Answers for this pack: hoodie/jacket = jbib (11); pants/jeans = lowr (4); chain/necklace = teef (7), NOT accs (8) — accs is the undershirt layer. Sources agreeing on teef=necklace: lucienlmy/5mod-tutorials table ("PV_COMP_TEEF | 7. Accessories | Teeth/Scarf/Necklace", "PV_COMP_ACCS | 8. Undershirts"), SOZ-FiveM-Server soz_clothes README ("teef Assesories 7", "accs undershirt 8"), and gta5-mods chain mods that ship as teef_0XX (search snippet only, page blocked). The enum labels TEETH/ACCESSORIES are legacy names and are misleading; the ghermans gist that lists slot 7 as "Eyes" is wrong/outdated.

Native parameters (citizenfx/natives): drawableId = "The drawable id that is going to be set", textureId = "The texture id of the drawable" (0 = texture letter a, 1 = b, ...), paletteId = "0 to 3" (normally 0 or 2). Props (hats, glasses, etc.) are a separate system (SET_PED_PROP_INDEX, p_ prefixed files) and are not involved for jacket/pants/chain.
ytd_naming:
A) REPLACEMENT (override a vanilla drawable) — grammar verified from CodeWalker MetaTypes.cs (GetTexturePrefix/GetTextureSuffix/GetDrawableName) and from real files in Zerofour04/FiveM-ClothingPack/stream:

  <pedModel>^<comp>_diff_<DDD>_<letter>_<race>.ytd     e.g. mp_m_freemode_01^jbib_diff_000_a_uni.ytd
  <pedModel>^<comp>_<DDD>_<u|r>.ydd                     e.g. mp_m_freemode_01^jbib_000_u.ydd

 - pedModel: mp_m_freemode_01 (male) / mp_f_freemode_01 (female). '^' separates ped from component.
 - comp: head|berd|hair|uppr|lowr|hand|feet|teef|accs|task|decl|jbib.
 - _diff_ = diffuse (colour) texture; the normal/spec maps for MP freemode clothing are embedded inside the .ydd (jbib_normal_000 / jbib_spec_000 — Sollumz wiki), not in the YTD.
 - DDD = drawable index, 3 digits zero-padded (CodeWalker: DrawableIndex.ToString("000")); it is the drawableId you pass to SetPedComponentVariation.
 - letter = texture variant = textureId; CodeWalker: alphas[texnum % 26] over "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz", so a=0, b=1 ... z=25 (max 26 per drawable).
 - race suffix comes from CPVTextureData.texId in the ped .ymt (CodeWalker switch, verified): 0=uni (universal), 1=whi (white), 2=bla (black), 3=chi (chinese), 4=lat (latino), 5=ara (arab), 8=kor (korean), 10=pak (pakistani), default->whi. Ids 6/7/9 are not in CodeWalker's switch (community lists them as bal/jam/ita — NOT verified). Clothing that shows no skin uses uni.
 - .ydd suffix comes from PropType (CodeWalker): 0="u" (universal), 1="r" (race-specific), 2/3="m" (unknown, CodeWalker comments "what do these mean?"). 5mod-tutorials: "Components have a _u suffix for universal or _r for race." Rule of thumb: _u.ydd pairs with _uni.ytd; _r.ydd pairs with race textures such as _whi (gtaforums snippet, page blocked).
 - IMPORTANT: items that were added by a GTA DLC are NOT under the bare prefix; the DLC pack name is part of the ped name. Verified examples: mp_m_freemode_01_male_heist^berd_016_u, mp_m_freemode_01_mp_m_heist3^berd_009_u (ONX_ES README), mp_f_freemode_01_mp_f_bikerdlc_01^hair_006_u.ydd, mp_f_freemode_01_mp_f_importexport_01^hair_003_u.ydd (Zerofour04). Find the correct pack name with OpenIV/CodeWalker in x64v.rpf\models\cdimages\streamedpeds_mp.rpf (base) or update\x64\dlcpacks\<dlc>\...\<dlc>_streamedpeds / _male / _female rpfs.
 - A texture-only replacement ships just the .ytd(s) with the vanilla name; keep the vanilla .ydd. Ship every letter the vanilla ymt declares for that drawable (a, b, c ...), otherwise the missing variants break.

B) ADD-ON pack (new drawables under your own dlcName) — verified from drkkkkkk/StaffHoodie, TimyStream/fivem-clothing-addon-template, FjamZoo/clothing_tool layout doc and 80+ manifests found by GitHub code search:

  <resource>/
    fxmanifest.lua
    mp_m_freemode_01_<dlcName>.meta            (ShopPedApparel; some packs name it ..._shop.meta — the official example is dlc_mpimportexport:/common/data/mp_m_freemode_01_impexp_shop.meta)
    stream/
      mp_m_freemode_01_<dlcName>.ymt           (ped variation info: components/drawables/aTexData; numAvailTex per component)
      mp_m_freemode_01_<dlcName>/
        mp_m_freemode_01_<dlcName>^jbib_000_u.ydd
        mp_m_freemode_01_<dlcName>^jbib_diff_000_a_uni.ytd
        mp_m_freemode_01_<dlcName>^jbib_diff_000_b_uni.ytd  (extra colour variants)
        mp_m_freemode_01_<dlcName>^lowr_000_u.ydd + ..._diff_000_a_uni.ytd
        mp_m_freemode_01_<dlcName>^teef_000_u.ydd + ..._diff_000_a_uni.ytd
      pedalternatevariations.meta               (optional, CAlternateVariations)
      mp_creaturemetadata_<name>.ymt            (optional; only if creatureMetaData/expressionMods are used)

 StaffHoodie concrete names: dlcName mp_m_staffhoodie -> fullDlcName mp_m_freemode_01_mp_m_staffhoodie; stream/mp_m_freemode_01_mp_m_staffhoodie.ymt; stream/mp_m_freemode_01_mp_m_staffhoodie/mp_m_freemode_01_mp_m_staffhoodie^jbib_000_u.ydd and ^jbib_diff_000_a_uni.ytd. Convention: dlcName is prefixed mp_m_/mp_f_ (mp_m_staffhoodie, mp_f_cherrypack, mp_m_tays_cluckinbellcloth ...).

 Shop meta (verified XML from StaffHoodie):
  <ShopPedApparel>
    <pedName>mp_m_freemode_01</pedName>
    <dlcName>mp_m_staffhoodie</dlcName>
    <fullDlcName>mp_m_freemode_01_mp_m_staffhoodie</fullDlcName>
    <eCharacter>SCR_CHAR_MULTIPLAYER</eCharacter>
    <creatureMetaData>MP_CreatureMetadata_StaffHoodie</creatureMetaData>
    <pedOutfits/> <pedComponents/> <pedProps/>
  </ShopPedApparel>
 creatureMetaData names an mp_creaturemetadata_*.ymt in stream/ (a real example exists: NaturalClothing/stream/[Grota]/mp_creaturemetadata_kit_tropa_grota_as.ymt). Per cfx-forum snippets (page blocked, NOT verified): it is only needed when the ymt uses expressionMods (heels, hiding hair under hats) and can be left empty otherwise. pedalternatevariations.meta (verified XML) lists <switches> that swap alternate drawables of other components when your add-on item (sourceAssets dlcNameHash=mp_m_staffhoodie, component 11, index 0) is worn — used e.g. for sleeve/arm alternates; exact semantics of component/alt values NOT verified.
 Add-on drawable numbering starts at 000 inside the pack; in game the drawable ids are appended after vanilla ones (well known, NOT re-verified here). gizzdev/gtautil `genpeddefs --fivem` can generate the ymt/meta/manifest from numbered folders (verified README).
fxmanifest:
Official definitions (citizenfx/fivem-docs resource-manifest/_index.md, verified): fx_version "Defines the supported functionality for the resource" — cerulean (2020-05, current) / bodacious / adamant; game: gta5 "Runs on FiveM" (games { 'gta5' } is the alternate form, used by Zerofour04); files: "Adds the specified file to the resource packfile, to be downloaded by clients upon loading the resource."; data_file: "Adds a data file of a specified type to the game extra content system." e.g. data_file 'VEHICLE_METADATA_FILE' 'myvehicles.meta'; this_is_a_map: "Marks this resource as being a GTA map, and reloads the map storage when the resource gets loaded." (this_is_a_map 'yes' -- can be any value). Beginner-series part-4 (verified): "Move any game asset files into the stream folder to ensure the files load properly." — anything in stream/ is streamed automatically and does NOT need to be listed in files{}.

1) Minimal manifest for a REPLACEMENT texture pack (verified working shape: Zerofour04/FiveM-ClothingPack ships only this plus stream/):
fx_version 'cerulean'
game 'gta5'
author 'you'
description 'Jacket / pants / chain retextures'
version '1.0.0'
-- put the .ytd (and optional .ydd) files in stream/; no files{} or data_file needed

2) Minimal manifest for an ADD-ON clothing pack (verified: TimyStream template + StaffHoodie + dozens of packs found via code search):
fx_version 'cerulean'
game 'gta5'
files {
  'mp_m_freemode_01_mp_m_mypack.meta',
  'stream/pedalternatevariations.meta'   -- only if you ship one
}
data_file 'SHOP_PED_APPAREL_META_FILE' 'mp_m_freemode_01_mp_m_mypack.meta'
data_file 'ALTERNATE_VARIATIONS_FILE' 'stream/pedalternatevariations.meta'   -- optional
-- add a second pair of files/data_file lines for mp_f_freemode_01_mp_f_mypack.meta if you ship female
-- the .ymt, .ydd, .ytd (and mp_creaturemetadata_*.ymt) go in stream/ and are not declared

Official data-file types (fivem-docs data-files.md, verified): SHOP_PED_APPAREL_META_FILE -> mounter CExtraMetaDataFileMounter, example dlc_mpimportexport:/common/data/mp_m_freemode_01_impexp_shop.meta; ALTERNATE_VARIATIONS_FILE -> CPedVariationStreamFileMounter, example dlc_mpbattlecrc:/common/data/pedalternatevariations.meta; PED_METADATA_FILE is for peds.meta (new ped models), NOT for clothing shop metas — using the wrong type makes the items silently not appear (snippet from fivemx, page blocked).

this_is_a_map pitfalls: it is for ymap/ytyp map resources only; a clothing pack must not set it. Because it "reloads the map storage when the resource gets loaded", adding it to non-map resources (some copy-pasted clothing manifests do) causes a needless map-storage reload; community reports of slower joins/streaming glitches were NOT verifiable (sources blocked). Other pitfalls: the meta file must be in files{} AND referenced by data_file (both lines); lua54 'yes' is optional; file names inside stream/ must be unique across all resources on the server (duplicate names collide — community knowledge); Zerofour04's README states streaming clothes requires a Cfx.re Element Club Argentum key (FiveM policy, reported by that README, not re-verified on docs.fivem.net).
texture_format:
YTD = RAGE texture dictionary holding DirectX block-compressed textures. Formats CodeWalker reads/writes for YTD via DDS (DDSIO.cs, verified): BC1_UNORM=DXT1, BC2=DXT3, BC3_UNORM=DXT5, BC4=ATI1, BC5=ATI2, BC7; mip count is taken from the DDS header (dwMipMapCount), so the DDS must already contain the mip chain.

Recommendation for clothing diffuse (_diff_) textures:
 - DXT1/BC1 (4 bpp) when the texture has no alpha — typical for jacket, pants, chain colour maps (ONX_ES pack ships "Resolution: 1024x1024, DDS Format: DXT1"; verified README).
 - DXT5/BC3 (8 bpp) when you need an alpha channel (cut-outs, semi-transparent parts). BC7 (8 bpp, higher quality) is also accepted and used by some creators (ONX_ES "DDS Format: BC7").
 - Always square power-of-two sizes and a full mipmap chain (Sollumz wiki troubleshooting: "Your diffuse is not square or not Power-of-2 (256x256 or 512x512 etc)"). Common clothing sizes observed: 512x512, 1024x1024, 1024x2048, 2048x2048 (FjamZoo clothing_tool doc); 1024x1024 is the usual target for clothing.
 - Keep the same compression the original texture used when replacing (modding-forum snippet, page blocked).
 - Texture name inside the YTD: keep it identical to the file name without extension (e.g. jbib_diff_000_a_uni), one texture per YTD. Supporting evidence: VogueV README step "IMPORTANT: Keep the exact same texture name"; CodeWalker Ped.cs looks the dictionary up by JenkHash of the lower-cased name and then takes Textures.data_items[0] with the comment "should only be one in this dict". Whether the game engine itself matches by texture name could not be verified from engine source — matching the name is the safe convention.
 - Normal (_normal_) and specular (_spec_) maps are embedded in the .ydd for MP freemode clothing; if you see a checkered overlay one is missing (Sollumz wiki). Not part of the texture-only package.

Importing with OpenIV (steps consolidated from several GitHub READMEs, verified): Tools > ASI Manager not needed; click "Edit mode" -> open the .ytd (Texture Editor opens) -> select the texture -> "Replace" -> pick your .dds (or .png; OpenIV converts and offers compression/mipmap options when the input is not DDS — modding-forum snippet, page blocked) -> Close and Save. New dictionary: with Edit mode on, right-click > New > Texture Dictionary (.ytd), then Import (snippet). Importing with CodeWalker: start CodeWalker with the 'explorer' argument (RPF Explorer, "an interface much like OpenIV" — CodeWalker README), enable Edit mode, open the .ytd, then replace/import the texture (drag & drop DDS) and save; CodeWalker can also export/import XML with a folder of DDS files. Suggested DDS authoring: Photoshop/GIMP/paint.net DDS exporters or texconv, BC1/BC3 with mipmaps generated.
addon_vs_replace:
REPLACEMENT: name your files exactly like an existing vanilla asset (mp_m_freemode_01^jbib_diff_000_a_uni.ytd, or the DLC-prefixed name for DLC items); FiveM streams them over the originals. Pros: only stream/ + a 3-line manifest; no ymt/meta; works with any clothing menu because the drawable/texture ids don't change. Cons: you lose the vanilla item; two packs replacing the same name conflict; you cannot add extra texture letters beyond what the vanilla .ymt declares (numAvailTex) and you must ship every declared letter; for texture-only work you must keep the vanilla .ydd's UV layout (export the vanilla YTD as a template first). Best fit when the user just wants retextures of an existing jacket, pants and chain.

ADD-ON: your own dlcName -> new drawable ids appended to the ped, own .ymt (declares drawables and numAvailTex/aTexData per drawable, up to 26 letters a-z), ShopPedApparel .meta declared with data_file 'SHOP_PED_APPAREL_META_FILE', optional pedalternatevariations.meta ('ALTERNATE_VARIATIONS_FILE') and mp_creaturemetadata_*.ymt. Pros: nothing vanilla is overwritten, unlimited colour variants, no name collisions between packs (as long as dlcName is unique). Cons: needs the .ydd models (or a copy of the vanilla .ydd renamed into the pack), tooling to write the .ymt (gtautil genpeddefs --fivem, Durty Cloth Tool, alt:V cloth tool, CodeWalker XML), drawable ids differ per server load order, and per-component drawable counts are bounded by game limits (Durty docs snippet, page blocked). File names for add-ons carry the dlc: mp_m_freemode_01_<dlc>^jbib_000_u.ydd + mp_m_freemode_01_<dlc>^jbib_diff_000_a_uni.ytd.

Documentation guidance: state clearly which mode the package uses; for replacement list the vanilla target (component, drawable id, DLC prefix, letters replaced); for add-on list dlcName, ymt name, and the drawable/texture counts declared.
